title: The VLA/ALMA Nascent Disk and Multiplicity (VANDAM) Survey of Orion Protostars. I. Identifying and Characterizing the Protostellar Content of the OMC-2 FIR4 and OMC-2 FIR3 Regions
question: What is the protostellar content of OMC2-FIR4 and OMC2-FIR3 at ~40 AU resolution, and what is the nature (luminosity, outflow, hot-corino chemistry) of HOPS-108 and HOPS-370?

data.sensitivity: continuum ~0.31 mJy/beam; 12CO ~7.7 mJy/beam (1 km/s); 13CO ~33.3 mJy/beam (0.44 km/s)

what.value: Bolometric luminosities and classes of protostars (HOPS SED fits)

evidence.loc: 3.3 Dust Continuum Mass and Radius Estimates
evidence.quote: The luminosity is the L$_{bol}$ for each protostellar system measured from the SED (cite: furlan2016).

what.value: APEX 0.87 mm flux density 12.3 Jy in 19'' aperture

evidence.quote: The flux density measured by the APEX observations was 12.3 Jy in a 19$''$ aperture centered on HOPS-108.

evidence.loc: 3.3 Dust Continuum Mass and Radius Estimates
evidence.quote: We adopt $\kappa_{0.87mm}$ = 1.84 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ from (cite: ossenkopf1994) column 5

recipe.goal: Measure source positions and flux densities
recipe.method: Gaussian fits with imfit to continuum images
Isothermal optically thin M = D^2 F/(kappa B(T)), times 100 for gas; radius = HWHM x distance
key_parameters: T_dust = 43 K (L/Lsun)^0.25; L=1 Lsun if unmeasured
assumptions: D=400 pc; kappa0.87mm=1.84 cm2/g; beta=1 extrapolation to 9 mm; dust-to-gas 1:100

recipe.goal: Methanol rotation temperature and column density
recipe.method: Rotation diagram from three methanol transitions with line fluxes in 0.5'' (HOPS-108) and 0.75'' (HOPS-370) apertures
assumptions: Optically thin, lines from same physical structure; mean molecular weight 2.8

recipe.method: Thermal equilibrium dust heating at 50 AU radius for 120 K or 160 K; accretion luminosity L=GMMdot/R
assumptions: Evaporation temperature 120 K (160 K with ice mixtures); protostellar radii from Hartmann 1997 and Palla 1993

evidence.quote: Thus, we are only recovering $\sim$2% of the overall flux density from this region in our observations.
we derive rotation temperatures of 140 K and 129 K for HOPS-108 and HOPS-370, respectively
methanol column density of 4.3$\times$10$^{16}$ cm$^{-2}$ and 1.4$\times$10$^{17}$ cm$^{-2}$ for HOPS-108 and HOPS-370

answer_key.quantity: Luminosity needed to heat dust to 120 K at 50 AU

evidence.loc: 4.3 Origin and Implications of the Compact Methanol Emission
evidence.quote: the luminosity required to heat dust to this temperature at a radius of 50 AU is $\sim$86 L$_{\odot}$
The system velocity of HOPS-108 is found to be 12.6 km s$^{-1}$

Number of clean iterations and deconvolver settings
Line-free channel ranges for continuum and for continuum subtraction in the line cubes

Exact adopted flux density of J0510+1800 and the derived Band 3 to 7 spectral index

Rotation diagram fitting uncertainties and any beam/optical depth corrections
missing_for_reproduction: Self-calibration details and flux model for J0510+1800
Tobin et al. radiative transfer grid for T0
score_reason: Central parameters (robust, uv cuts, tapers, solints, CASA version) given, but several imaging and line analysis details absent.
